message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the two orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. In other words, it is the last common ancestor of all **placental mammals (Eutheria)**, which lived roughly 100–120 million years ago during the early Cretaceous. This ancestor gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.

The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). Both are mammals, but more specifically both are in the order Carnivora? No, zebra is in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). Lion is in order Carnivora. So their common ancestor would be at the level of the class Mammalia, maybe the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But perhaps they want the last common ancestor of the two species, which is the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae. That would be at the level of the order level: the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals except monotremes and marsupials. Actually, the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals (Eutheria). But we can be more precise: The last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But if we want a specific name, it's the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals. But maybe the answer: "The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived around 100 million years ago." Or "the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of all eutherian mammals." So answer accordingly.
